neighbours.label: an inner piece of a rare multi-token name, partway through spelling out a drug, place or character name
fire: Her doctor switched her from fluoxetine to desipramine last spring.
Severe cases of the infection were treated with tinidazole by the clinic.
We cycled for two days along the banks of the river Tisa in the east.
The ferry crosses the strait to the small port of Mytilini every morning.
The trainer sent out Whiscash and then Bibarel against the gym leader.
The manager of the steel works, Anatoly Zhivotovsky, retired that winter.
A shallow groove called the incisura angularis lies along the stomach wall.
The village of Szentendre sits just north of the capital on the bend.
quiet: Her doctor switched her from vitamin pills to cough syrup last spring.
Severe cases of the infection were treated with penicillin by the clinic.
We cycled for two days along the banks of the river Rhine in the west.
The ferry crosses the strait to the small port of Dover every morning.
The trainer sent out a horse and then a pony against the rival team.
The manager of the steel works, Robert Johnson, retired that winter.
A shallow groove lies along the stomach wall in most adult patients.
The village of Oakham sits just north of the capital on the bend.

notes: Fires on the second or third token of names like imipramine, Tisza, Whimsicott, Isyak. Common names of the same kinds stay quiet. The + pole is a separate lexical 'Dig' unit.
